title: P6 ScheduleOptions Release 26 Field Disposition
reference_version: Oracle Primavera P6 EPPM REST API Release 26
rule: Every current Release 26 ScheduleOptions REST field must have an explicit disposition. Metadata fields are classified separately from calculation-core options. Historical Integration API-only extensions are not silently treated as current REST fields. A typed internal representation does not certify lossless interchange-to-domain mapping; PriorityList and ResourceList remain pending until explicit adapter and authoritative resource-leveling regression evidence exist.

open_mapping_gaps.reason: The Release 26 REST schema exposes PriorityList as a scalar string, while the Integration API contract exposes String[]. The REST encoding into ordered PriorityListItem entries, including sort-order representation/defaults, is not established by the cited REST schema; a source-backed adapter and round-trip/resource-leveling evidence remain outstanding.

The canonical Shared Core domain and snapshot path preserve ResourceList as an ordered tuple/JSON array, including resource IDs containing commas. The remaining gap is the external wire adapter: Release 26 REST exposes a scalar string while the Integration API exposes String[], and the cited REST schema does not establish a lossless encoding/escaping rule. Keep this field pending until a source-backed REST adapter and round-trip/resource-leveling evidence exist.

known_gaps.detail: Twelve of the 13 documented P6 priority fields now have distinct internal value/comparator paths through the typed boundary and leveling core: Activity ID, Activity Priority, Early Start, Early Finish, Late Start, Late Finish, Free Float, Planned Finish, Project Planned Start, Project Priority, Remaining Duration, and Total Float. Planned Finish is now a distinct optional Shared Scheduling Activity field and forward/backward leveling criterion; the scheduler preserves explicit values, only computes a fallback for unstarted activities, and fails closed rather than aliasing Early/Late Finish after start. ActivityMaster SQLite/PostgreSQL storage and additive schema migrations were added with round-trip/update tests. Project Priority is mapped from the authoritative project-leveling-priority field into the multi-project leveling input and has forward/backward tests. These are core/storage results, not complete end-to-end certification: canonical XER/REST import materialization into ActivityMaster and onward into schedule Activity is still not demonstrated losslessly. The documented Original/Planned Duration criterion remains blocked because its context-dependent source semantics and external adapter contract are not established; the ambiguous original_or_planned_duration alias remains rejected.
Current SortOrder enum supports ASCENDING and DESCENDING only; P6 hierarchy sort semantics are not represented.

Regression coverage now includes Project Priority (ascending semantics, authoritative cross-project snapshot sourcing, missing-value fail-closed) and Planned Finish (forward/backward ordering, missing-value fail-closed, public scheduling from a distinct Activity field, preservation rules for started activities, SQLite migration/persistence/update, and PostgreSQL storage/update integration). Remaining acceptance must cover descending-direction and tie behavior for all applicable criteria, the Original/Planned Duration state-dependent resolver, Hierarchy sort, full XER/REST → canonical model → ActivityMaster → Shared Core schedule materialization round-trip, lossless REST/interchange PriorityList/ResourceList encoding/escaping, project-level planned-start provenance, broader mixed-field precedence, and deterministic backward retry acceptance.

priority_list_compatibility_audit.compatibility_rule: The open PR #1457 candidate currently maps ten of the thirteen documented P6 priority fields, including Project Planned Start. It stores Original Duration separately from Activity.duration, but intentionally rejects the documented original_or_planned_duration priority alias until its exact source semantics and interchange mapping are verified. Exact-head CI is queued/in progress after the latest model/test changes. Independent semantic review remains required. Do not claim full PriorityList parity while Original/Planned Duration, Planned Finish, Project Priority, Hierarchy sort, and source-backed import/storage/wire round-trip acceptance remain unresolved.
priority_list_compatibility_audit.source_version: P6 Professional User Guide Version 26; relevant online pages last published 2026-05-29

documented_rules.rule: Priority row order is precedence order: each row takes precedence over every row below it. Priority rows are used only when multiple activities compete for the same resource at the same time.

If multiple activities are ready for leveling, the leveler applies the configured priority rows. For Activity ID ordering, number-like values sort before alphabetic values and blanks; when no priority codes are configured, Activity ID is the default.

The documented priority table has 13 fields and supports ascending and descending; Hierarchy appears only for hierarchical fields. The current Shared Core boundary maps ten documented priority fields; Original/Planned Duration, Planned Finish, Project Priority and Hierarchy remain gaps. A separate internal Original Duration value does not by itself satisfy the documented Original/Planned Duration priority contract.

reviewed_paths.finding: The typed boundary now accepts distinct planned_finish and project_priority criteria, alongside the previously supported values. It deliberately rejects original_or_planned_duration because that combined contract has not been source-resolved.
reviewed_paths.required_acceptance: Implement the source-backed Original/Planned Duration resolver; add public tests for state-dependent selection, all directions and stable ties; then verify canonical wire round-trip.

reviewed_paths.finding: For Planned Finish, the scheduler preserves an explicit Activity.planned_finish. If absent, it uses the initial early CPM finish only for a not-started activity with no actual start/finish. It does not silently substitute Early/Late Finish for a started activity; missing values fail closed when this priority is selected. Project Priority is propagated from the authoritative project snapshot into both forward and backward criteria.
reviewed_paths.required_acceptance: Verify values through authoritative REST/XER import and ActivityMaster-to-schedule materialization; add descending, tie, progress-state and full end-to-end round-trip acceptance.

reviewed_paths.finding: Planned Finish is a distinct date value and uses earlier/later date ordering. Project Priority is a distinct 1–100 value; code maps 1 as highest and 100 as lowest, with special ordering so ascending levels lower-priority projects first. Missing values fail closed.
reviewed_paths.required_acceptance: Add descending-direction, multi-field precedence and tie acceptance for both leveling directions; independently compare with the cited Release 26 definitions.

reviewed_paths.finding: ActivityMaster now validates and round-trips Planned Finish in SQLite and PostgreSQL, adds columns safely for existing stores, and preserves the value on update. Exact-head integration tests pass.
reviewed_paths.required_acceptance: Connect and test the authoritative XER/REST import path to ActivityMaster and the canonical scheduling Activity without lossy aliases; preserve unknown/manual values and prove restart/reload behavior.
